comparator.name: Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology
comparator.sourceNotes: The normalized target merges English and Dutch language registrations. The adopted OER lists English first. Year 1 has seven 6-EC named courses, 9 EC of Ethnographic Research Methodology 1 and 6+3 EC of two masterclasses. Year 2 has six 6-EC subject courses, two 6-EC masterclasses and two 6-EC restricted Social Sciences for Society choices; representative broad options are instantiated. Year 3 has 30 EC genuinely open elective/minor space, two 6-EC compulsory courses and one 18-EC bachelor project. The public researcher, practitioner and creative profiles shape project presentation rather than forming separate credited tracks in the adopted OER.
components: Discovering Anthropology: Histories, Theories and Practices
Global Religion in the Digital Age
Beyond Gender Inequalities (restricted Social Sciences for Society choice)
Selected from the formal first choice group; Confronting Commodity Chains and Towards Better Care and Welfare are alternatives, not additional requirements.
The Human Dimension of Sustainable Development: From Ideal to Reality (restricted Social Sciences for Society choice)
Selected from the formal second choice group; AI & Society and Social Entrepreneurship are alternatives, not additional requirements.
Genuinely open first-semester minor, internship, study abroad or approved electives.
Fieldwork-based thesis and a profile-appropriate research, policy or creative output within this single credited project.

routeSelection.basis: The merged normalized target covers Dutch and English tracks of the same bachelor. The adopted 2026–27 OER lists English first; this neutral tie-break selects the English route independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Culture, inequality and visual social inquiry
alternatives.concept: Combines sociology, global and Indigenous histories, political questions, qualitative research, heritage and visual media to examine culture, identity and inequality. UCR offers related social and cultural inquiry, but no dedicated sequence of ethnographic fieldwork or the VU 18-EC anthropology project.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule integrates interpretive social inquiry with power, development, historical and audiovisual representation.
progression: Six four-course semesters in Fall 2026–Spring 2029, PPD in Year 1, at least six 300-level courses, verified term offerings and earlier formal prerequisites against the enriched UCR workbook. Introductory social science and methods precede advanced work where feasible.

alternatives.label: Development, governance and social justice
alternatives.concept: Emphasizes the political, economic and legal institutions that shape inequality, migration and social change, while retaining qualitative social research and cultural analysis. It translates anthropological questions toward policy and governance without claiming a professional anthropology credential.
alternatives.labelReason: Economics, political philosophy, comparative constitutional law and EU law make development and governance the organizing application.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses change: Introduction to Economics, Introduction to Political Philosophy, Comparative Constitutional Law and Foundations of European Union Law replace Introduction to Film & Media, Histories of Gender, Media & the Environment and The Documentary. This moves 30 EC from cultural and visual analysis toward institutions, economics and policy.
progression: Six four-course semesters in Fall 2026–Spring 2029, PPD in Year 1, at least six 300-level courses, verified term offerings and earlier formal prerequisites against the enriched UCR workbook. Introductory social science and methods precede advanced work where feasible.

selection.assessment: The first path spans social and cultural analysis with visual inquiry. A four-course-distinct development and governance route is feasible. A third religion-centered anthropology path lacks a dedicated UCR religion and ethnographic sequence, while a criminology combination would displace the core anthropology response; neither supports a new defensible 24-course path. Creative and media combinations are already substantively represented in the first path.

notes.text: VU’s English route includes a 9-EC first ethnographic-methods unit, further fieldwork training, anthropology masterclasses, two restricted social-science choices and an 18-EC fieldwork-based bachelor project, with 30 EC of open elective space. UCR combines social science, history, cultural studies and media, but does not reproduce that sustained ethnographic training or the independent anthropology thesis.
